scope: Selected source plus all 27 stored classification prediction sets from four completed episodes. Independent point-loss recomputation only; recorded bootstrap is not rerun. No candidate import/execution or checkpoint deserialization. No counterfactual rollout or claim that an earlier audit would have occurred. TREC includes repetition 0 only.

rows.model_authored_rationale:
TREC text classification: beat the word-TFIDF LinearSVC reference by (a) fusing word
1-2gram, character_wb 2-5gram and explicit question-head (first 1/2/3 token) features into a
single sparse representation, (b) selecting the regularisation / block weighting / model
ensemble by group-aware cross-validation on the training rows only, and (c) optionally adding a
transductive self-training round over the unlabelled features given at prediction time.

Rationale (exploratory, validated only by internal group CV here):
- TREC labels are driven largely by the interrogative head ("what kind of", "how many",
  "who"); explicit head tokens give the linear model unambiguous high-weight features that
  1-2 word n-grams dilute.  Character n-grams add robustness to rare content words.
- The two reference arms (word-only 0.1542, char-only 0.1567 dev error) are close, which
  suggests they are partly complementary; averaging calibrated decision functions of both
  families is a cheap variance reduction.
- All selection uses GroupKFold over api.train_groups (the declared generalisation protocol);
  development labels are never used.  Vectorizer vocabulary/idf is fitted on train+development
  *features* only (unsupervised, no labels).
Limitations: model/ensemble selection over many candidates on ~3.8k CV rows can overfit the
selection by a few tenths of a percent; self-training is enabled only when it improves CV by a
clear margin.  No pretrained weights or external data are used.

selected_training_findings.limitations: CV selection over many candidates can optimistically bias the reported CV error; development labels were never used; vectorizer vocabulary fitted on train+development features only.

recorded_comparison.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.
Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.

rows.model_authored_rationale:
TREC: engineered sparse linear models + from-scratch subword BiGRU, ensembled by grouped CV.

Rationale (exploratory, unverified). Parent b0-s0 used a stacked sparse model: word
1-3grams, char_wb 2-5grams and structural tokens (wh-word, head noun and similar
cues) with a LinearSVC. It improved development loss (0.1346 vs 0.1542) but did not
qualify on confirmation. With 812 confirmation rows the standard error is about
0.013, so a larger real gain is needed.

This step makes two changes:
 1. Richer structure tokens:
    - char 3/4-grams of the heuristic head noun, so unseen heads such as
      -ist/-er/-ity words can generalize;
    - a what+aux+length cue for definition (DESC) questions;
    - a plural-head flag.
 2. A second, heterogeneous learner trained on the GPU from scratch. It is a BiGRU
    over word embeddings plus fastText-style hashed char n-gram embeddings, using
    crc32 so the hashing is deterministic, and a bag of the structure tokens.
    It is trained over several seeds.
The log-probabilities of SVC (softmax of the margins), LR and the NN are mixed.
Mixing weights come from a small grid on out-of-fold predictions under GroupKFold
on the training groups. The pure linear models are included in that grid, so the
ensemble falls back to them if the NN does not help in CV.

Limitations: weights are chosen on the same folds that are reported, so there is
mild optimism. The TF-IDF vocabulary uses train plus unlabeled development text.

selected_training_findings.limitations: Mixing weights and SVC config were selected on the same grouped CV folds (optimistic). TF-IDF vocab fit on train+unlabeled dev text. NN CV used fewer seeds than the final ensemble.

recorded_comparison.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.
Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.

rows.model_authored_rationale:
KMNIST: deep ensemble of small residual CNNs with GPU affine augmentation + cutout, plus shift TTA.

Rationale (exploratory, unverified until measured): the common reference is a single
CIFAR-style ResNet trained with pad-and-crop only, reaching 0.65% development error.
Two well-established, low-risk sources of further error reduction on small-data
character recognition are (a) richer label-preserving geometric augmentation
(small rotation / scale / shear / translation, which respect KMNIST semantics and
never use horizontal flips) combined with cutout, and (b) averaging softmax outputs
over an ensemble of independently seeded networks and a few small-translation
test-time views.  Both are variance-reduction mechanisms rather than new inductive
biases, so they should compound with the reference recipe rather than trade off
against it.  Training 12k 28x28 images is cheap, so within the 900 s train limit we
can fit several networks instead of one, which is the main expected gain.

Implementation notes / limitations:
 - No horizontal flip anywhere (augmentation or TTA), per task contract.
 - All 12k training rows are used for fitting; no internal validation split is held
   out, so the reported training error is in-sample and is NOT a generalization
   estimate.  Model selection is by construction (fixed recipe), not by score.
 - Number of ensemble members adapts to measured wall-clock speed on the shared GPU;
   the cosine LR schedule is driven by max(epoch progress, time progress) so a slow
   GPU still yields fully annealed models.
 - State dicts (CPU tensors) are stored in the model dict; the architecture is
   rebuilt at prediction time from this same module, so no mutable module globals
   are relied upon.

selected_training_findings.limitations: No held-out internal validation; train error is in-sample and optimistic. Member count depends on measured GPU speed, so the artifact is not bitwise reproducible. No development labels were used.

recorded_comparison.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.

rows.model_authored_rationale:
KMNIST: ensemble of affine-augmented residual CNNs, plus the parent reference net.

Rationale (exploratory, unverified): the reference is one ResNet-style CNN trained
with crop-only augmentation. Its development error is 0.65%, about 13 errors on
2000 images. At that level, averaging several independently seeded networks
usually removes a share of the remaining idiosyncratic errors. Two further changes
should also help:
- Stroke-geometry augmentation: small rotation, scale, shear and translation,
  plus mild cutout. No flips, because reflection changes KMNIST classes.
- Light shift test-time averaging.
The parent reference net is loaded from parent_dir and reused as one ensemble
member, which costs no training time. Each member follows a time-based cosine
schedule, so training finishes inside the limit even if the shared GPU is slow.
No development labels are used. Limitation: no internal held-out estimate is
computed; all training rows are used for fitting.

selected_training_findings.limitations: No labeled internal validation; agreement is label-free.
